rawFindings.title: Incorrect comment in encoder writeObject function
rawFindings.explanation: The comment above the changed line incorrectly refers to 'java.utils.HashMap', which is a non-existent package, instead of the correct 'java.util.HashMap'. The actual code correctly references javaObject.DEFAULT_CLASSNAME.map. This discrepancy can confuse readers.
rawFindings.suggestion: Update the comment to correctly state 'java.util.HashMap' instead of 'java.utils.HashMap'.

rawFindings.title: Incorrect class name check for java.util.HashMap in writeObject
rawFindings.explanation: In the original code, the condition checking if obj.$class equals either javaObject.DEFAULT_CLASSNAME.map or javaObject.DEFAULT_CLASSNAME.iMap was used to decide an empty className for writing untyped hash maps. The patch changes this to only check if obj.$class equals javaObject.DEFAULT_CLASSNAME.map, removing the second condition. However, javaObject.DEFAULT_CLASSNAME.iMap ('java.util.Map') is a valid map class name that should be treated similarly. Removing this breaks encoding for objects wi
rawFindings.suggestion:
Restore the original condition to check both javaObject.DEFAULT_CLASSNAME.map and javaObject.DEFAULT_CLASSNAME.iMap when setting className to empty string for map objects, as in:
className = obj.$class === javaObject.DEFAULT_CLASSNAME.map || obj.$class === javaObject.DEFAULT_CLASSNAME.iMap ? '' : obj.$class;

The new line removes that check, which may change behavior when an object with class 'java.util.Map' is passed, leading to a different handling. rawFindings.suggestion: Restore the check for `javaObject.DEFAULT_CLASSNAME.iMap` in the condition to preserve previous behavior, and correct the comment to 'java.util.HashMap'.
